value.content: {"id": "portswigger_websockets", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "websockets", "category": "PortSwigger Web Security: WebSockets Security", "name": "Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH) & Message Tampering Methodology", "cwe": "CWE-1385", "owasp_category": "A01:2021 - Broken Access Control", "signals": ["ws_upgrade_without_csrf_protection", "origin_header_not_validated_in_ws", "unencrypted_ws_protocol", "unsanitized_ws_message_rendering", "ws_sql_or_xss_injection"], "verification_strategy": "Inspect WebSocket handshake requests (GET /chat with Upgrade: websocket). Verify whether the handshake checks the Origin header or includes anti-CSRF tokens. Audit bidirectional frames for SQL injection, XSS, or unauthorized message manipulation.", "evidence_requirements": ["cross_origin_handshake_acceptance", "origin_reflection_in_ws", "tainted_ws_frame_trace"], "tools": [{"tool": "BrowserAgent (WebSocket Audit)", "cmd": "BrowserAgent.monitor_websockets(url)", "desc": "Interprets client-side WebSocket messages and evaluates origin validation"}, {"tool": "wscat", "cmd": "wscat -c 'wss://example.com/chat' -H 'Origin: https://attacker.com'", "desc": "Tests cross-origin WebSocket handshake acceptance"}], "remediation": "Validate the Origin header strictly during the WebSocket upgrade handshake. Implement anti-CSRF tokens in the initial handshake request or require unique authentication tokens per session.", "description": "PortSwigger WebSockets labs cover intercepting and modifying WebSocket messages, Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH) to exfiltrate private conversation history, and exploiting XSS via WebSocket message rendering."}
